lessons.title: Why web is the biggest attack surface
lessons.body: Most organisations expose far more web than anything else, and web bugs are where a database background pays off fastest. Set up a deliberately vulnerable target first (OWASP Juice Shop or DVWA in Docker) so every tool below has something legal to hit.

tools.name: Burp Suite (Community)
tools.what: An intercepting proxy: it sits between your browser and a site so you can read and modify every request. The free edition does manual testing and repeating requests; Pro adds an automated scanner. This is the center of most web testing.
tools.legal: Only run this against machines you own or have explicit written permission to test. Scanning or attacking other systems is illegal.
tools.install: Download from PortSwigger; bundled in Kali. Pair with PortSwigger's free Web Security Academy.
try: # point your browser's proxy at 127.0.0.1:8080, then browse your local Juice Shop
tools.exercise: Intercept a login on your local Juice Shop, change one field, and forward it. Watch how the server reacts - that is the whole game of web testing.

tools.name: ffuf
tools.what: A fast web fuzzer: it requests many paths/parameters from a wordlist to discover hidden pages, directories, or parameters a site did not advertise.
tools.legal: Only run this against machines you own or have explicit written permission to test. Scanning or attacking other systems is illegal.
tools.exercise: Fuzz your local lab app for hidden directories. Compare what ffuf finds to what the site links to - the gap is attack surface.

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.what: Automates finding and exploiting SQL injection: detects injectable parameters, fingerprints the DBMS, and can dump data. With ten years of SQL Server you will understand exactly what it does under the hood - and why parameterised queries stop it.
tools.legal: Only run this against machines you own or have explicit written permission to test. Scanning or attacking other systems is illegal.
tools.install: `sudo apt install sqlmap` or `pip install sqlmap`.
tools.exercise: Stand up a tiny vulnerable PHP+SQL app (or DVWA) on localhost, let sqlmap find the injection, then rewrite the query with parameters and watch sqlmap fail. That before/after is a great blog post.
